record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.context_brief: future reach and reliability of current results
record.original_question: Can the parts of the QCD phase diagram that are currently out of reach become accessible in the future, and are some of the results currently believed to be correct actually still vulnerable to revision? This is the paper’s broad meta-level open question about the long-term reliability and eventual completeness of present finite-density lattice QCD knowledge.

evidence.quote: Perhaps the parameter regions currently out of reach can be studied in the future, or perhaps the results currently believed to be correct turn out to be wrong.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at finite baryon density, formulated on a Euclidean spacetime lattice with quark chemical potential μ ≠ 0. Because the Euclidean fermion determinant det M(μ) is in general complex for μ ≠ 0, direct importance sampling Monte Carlo simulation is obstructed by the so-called sign problem, and large regions of the (T, μ) phase diagram — in particular the conjectured QCD critical end point and the cold, dense regime relevant to neutron-star matter — are currently inaccessible to fully controlled first-principles lattice computations. Existing partial results rely on techniques such as Taylor expansion around μ = 0, analytic continuation from imaginary chemical potential, reweighting, the complex Langevin equation, Lefschetz-thimble methods, and dual/worldline reformulations, each with its own systematic uncertainties.

Address the following meta-level question regarding the long-term completeness and reliability of finite-density lattice QCD:

(a) Determine whether the regions of the QCD phase diagram in the (T, μ) plane that are presently out of reach of controlled lattice simulations — including a rigorous determination of the existence and location of the conjectured critical end point and of the phase structure at low temperature and large baryon chemical potential — can in principle be made accessible by some future algorithmic or theoretical development that fully resolves the sign problem (or by a proof that no polynomial-time resolution exists, as for example under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions).

(b) Determine whether any of the finite-density lattice QCD results currently believed to be correct (such as the curvature of the pseudo-critical line near μ = 0, equation-of-state expansions, and bounds on the location of the critical end point obtained from Taylor coefficients or from imaginary-μ analytic continuation) are subject to revision when their as-yet-uncontrolled systematic errors (truncation of the Taylor series, ambiguities of analytic continuation, finite-volume and continuum-limit effects) are eventually brought under full control.

Provide either a rigorous resolution of (a) and (b), or a precise framework in which such a resolution can be formulated.
artifact.category_tag: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem
artifact.status_search_result: The sign problem in finite-density lattice QCD remains an outstanding open problem; no general controlled method exists for the cold, dense regime, and the existence/location of the QCD critical end point is still unresolved as of recent reviews and lattice conference proceedings. Complexity-theoretic results (Troyer–Wiese) suggest a generic resolution is unlikely, but partial progress continues via complex Langevin, Lefschetz thimbles, and Taylor/imaginary-μ methods.

status_evidence.title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Review enumerates open problems in finite-density lattice QCD and the sign problem, with substantial regions of the phase diagram still inaccessible.
status_evidence.claim: The sign problem and the inaccessibility of large regions of the QCD phase diagram remain open.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity and fundamental limitations to fermionic quantum Monte Carlo simulations (Troyer, Wiese)
status_evidence.snippet: A generic solution of the sign problem would imply NP-hard problems are solvable in polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: A fully general algorithmic resolution of the sign problem is widely believed to be impossible under standard complexity assumptions.
